bullet_points: Load the 10 galaxy and halo catalogs from the provided absolute paths.

Match each satellite galaxy to its host halo by finding the nearest halo center in 3D space (using a KD-tree or brute-force search) among halos whose virial mass matches the satellite's ln_M_h value within a small tolerance, accounting for periodic boundary conditions.
Compute and store the 3D offset vector (dx, dy, dz) and scalar radial distance r = |r_sat - r_halo| for each satellite.
Filter the data to isolate halos with M > 10^13 M_sun/h and satellites within the 1-halo regime (r < 5 Mpc/h).
Save the processed data as a structured NumPy array with fields: halo_mass, r_vir, r_sat, dx, dy, dz, ln_L, realization_id.
Print summary statistics: number of matched satellites per realization, number of halos above M_sat threshold, and mean number of satellites per qualifying halo.
Define 3 logarithmically spaced mass bins above M_sat = 10^13 M_sun/h.
Compute the empirical 3D radial density profile n(r|M_vir) normalized as a number density (satellites per unit volume shell) for each mass bin.
Calculate the mean and variance of these profiles across the 10 realizations.
Print bin populations and mean satellite counts per bin.
Save the resulting empirical profiles and their statistics to disk.
Implement the theoretical 1-halo satellite distribution model rho(r) proportional to r^-2 exp(-r / (alpha * R_vir)).
Fit the radial scale parameter alpha via MLE on individual satellite radial distances r/R_vir.
Separately fit M_min and alpha_sat by comparing observed mean satellite counts per halo mass bin against the HOD prediction N_sat(M) = (M/M_sat)^alpha_sat.
Print both sets of recovered parameters with uncertainties alongside ground-truth values.
Save the recovered parameters and model fit statistics.
sub_tasks.sub_task: Analytic Model Construction and Parameter Recovery

bullet_points: Compute the marked correlation function M(r) = [sum(m_i * m_j * w(r_ij))] / [sum(w(r_ij))] where m_i = L_i / <L> are normalized luminosity marks and w(r_ij) is a pair-counting weight.
Compare M(r) against the unmarked 2PCF xi(r) within the 1-halo regime (r < 5 Mpc/h).
Quantify the deviation from unity using the ratio M(r)/[1 + xi(r)].
Save the marked correlation results and diagnostic statistics.
Calculate residuals between observed 1-halo clustering and the analytic model.
Aggregate all results across the 10 realizations to define confidence intervals.

Generate a single multi-panel figure containing: (a) empirical radial profiles per mass bin with best-fit models, (b) M(r) vs. 1+xi(r), (c) radial profile residuals, and (d) a summary table of recovered vs. ground-truth HOD parameters.
Save all final numerical results and the multi-panel plot.
Synthesize findings from empirical radial profiles and analytic model fits.
Interpret the impact of the luminosity mark on spatial clustering statistics, referencing the M(r)/[1 + xi(r)] ratio.
Discuss limitations of the Neyman-Scott kernel based on 1-halo residual analysis.

Write the full Results section, including recovered values of alpha, M_min, alpha_sat (with mean/std), chi-squared/log-likelihood values, amplitude/scale of M(r) deviations, and quantitative residual amplitude, referencing each subplot panel (a-d) by letter.
